recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-32558 unless OO later requests additional non-normative UDI tutorial prose beyond the current Device element definition, comments, and generated mapping.
issue_request: FHIR-32558 was Published with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. The issue challenged Device.distinctIdentifier as possible extension territory; OO decided it should remain in core because it is integral to UDI production-identifier traceability, with clarification around biologicalSource naming, UDI guidance/mapping, no RIM mapping, and individual or grouped source traceability.
initial_application: No direct FHIR-32558-keyed source commit was found. Jira comments and OO minutes state the issue was applied through FHIR-34346. Commit 853c7334f534e4bc897b3169daee6139af1e149d changed Device.distinctIdentifier to Device.biologicalSource, changed it from string to Identifier, kept 0..1 cardinality, added DIC/traceability metadata, and removed the old mappings from that element pending later cleanup.
additional_context: FHIR-37199 later renamed biologicalSource to biologicalSourceEvent and expanded the shared traceability comment across Device, BiologicallyDerivedProduct, and NutritionProduct. FHIR-22834 and FHIR-51520 later updated the UDI mapping for Device.biologicalSourceEvent to distinct identification code / donation identification number wording. Related FHIR-34346, FHIR-37199, and FHIR-34421 already have combined-branch reconciliation commits.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Device StructureDefinition already contains Device.biologicalSourceEvent with Identifier type, 0..1 cardinality, DIC alias, expanded traceability comment, no RIM mapping, and explicit UDI mapping for DIC/DIN/source-origin traceability. The remaining distinctIdentifier hits are a migration mapping and a historical FHIR ModelInfo Library example, not current Device conformance source.
